furnace.afueNote: NRCan: gas furnaces from around 1970 ran at about 60%, mid-1980s models at 78 to 84%, condensing furnaces at 90 to 98%.

usRule.status: On June 8, 2026 the US Supreme Court set aside the appeals-court decision that had upheld the rule and sent the case back; the Department of Energy has said it is considering a delay to 2030. Until a court or the Department acts, the December 18, 2028 date stands.

ac.refrigerant: In the US, new residential systems made or imported since January 1, 2025 must use a refrigerant with a global warming potential of 700 or less (R-454B or R-32). On May 21, 2026 the EPA removed the deadline for installing older R-410A stock, so equipment made before 2025 can still be installed until it runs out.

thermostat.setbackNote: 3°C (about 5°F) lower for 8 hours overnight and 8 hours while the house is empty on a workday; heat pumps are limited to the 2°C NRCan advises.

filtration.wattsNote: Illustrative loads for the fan-cost table: read the wattage on your own furnace or cleaner and scale.
